I've hosted several dev and one prod server on AWS. No hardware costs, obviously, and excellent uptime and bandwidth. Downside is you pay for each hour and there's a lot of hours each month. Included in hourly costs is a fixed IP address and storage. You'll likely end up with far less processing power than your home server, but most of that power is overkill anyway.

The AWS billing dashboard is pretty good at helping you estimate your monthly costs at the start so you won't have surprises. Generic web hosting is much cheaper but you have little control over the server (no root/admin access).
